scenes.title: Kafka Architecture
scenes.subtitle: Brokers, KRaft, and the ZooKeeper it replaced
scenes.narration: Kafka's architecture is built from brokers that store data and a control plane that keeps the cluster coordinated.

scenes.title: The Building Blocks
bullets: Brokers store partitions and serve reads and writes
A cluster is many brokers working together
Metadata tracks topics, partitions, and leaders
A controller manages leadership and membership
scenes.narration: Brokers are the servers that store partition data and serve producer and consumer requests. A cluster is simply many brokers working together to share the load. Metadata records which topics and partitions exist and which broker leads each one. A special controller role manages leader election and cluster membership as brokers come and go.

scenes.title: ZooKeeper vs KRaft
scenes.narration: Historically Kafka relied on ZooKeeper, a separate distributed system that stored cluster metadata but added operational complexity. KRaft replaces it by managing metadata inside Kafka itself using the Raft consensus protocol. This removes an entire dependency, simplifies operations, and speeds up controller failover. Modern Kafka deployments run in KRaft mode by default.

scenes.title: How the Controller Keeps Order
scenes.narration: Suppose a broker fails. The controller detects the loss through missed heartbeats. It then elects new leaders for the partitions that broker had led, choosing from the in-sync replicas. Finally, updated metadata propagates to producers and consumers so they redirect to the new leaders, keeping the cluster available.

scenes.title: Inspecting the Cluster
scenes.code:
# List brokers and the controller (KRaft)
kafka-metadata-quorum.sh \
  --bootstrap-server localhost:9092 describe --status

# Show broker configs
kafka-broker-api-versions.sh \
  --bootstrap-server localhost:9092
scenes.narration: In KRaft mode you can inspect the metadata quorum to see the current controller and the state of the Raft log. The describe status command reports the leader, the followers, and how caught up they are. The second command lists the brokers and the API versions they support. These tools help you confirm the control plane is healthy.

scenes.text: Brokers hold the data; the controller keeps the cluster coordinated. KRaft folds that coordination into Kafka itself, retiring ZooKeeper.
scenes.narration: The takeaway is that brokers hold the data while the controller keeps the cluster coordinated. KRaft folds that coordination into Kafka itself, retiring the old ZooKeeper dependency.
